claims.text: An integrated in-situ high-temperature XRD-TGA method can simultaneously measure oxidation kinetics and phase evolution under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
The integrated method provides more accurate and dynamic insight than separate ex situ analyses.
A custom furnace with X-ray-transparent windows can support simultaneous TGA and XRD measurements in a controlled oxidizing atmosphere.
The proposed method can operate from 600°C to 1500°C under an oxidizing atmosphere.
XRD scan cycles of 1–5 minutes can capture transient oxidation and phase-transformation phenomena.
Formation and evolution of an oxidation scale cause changes in sample mass and phase structure.
Changes in XRD peak positions and intensities, together with the appearance of new peaks, can track phase evolution and transformations.
TGA records mass gain or loss associated with oxide formation.
In-situ XRD tracks the emergence and transformation of crystalline phases.
Simultaneous TGA and XRD data can correlate transient oxidation kinetics with structural phase changes.
Sequential measurements may miss dynamic interactions that simultaneous measurements can reveal.
The integrated experiment will show a clear correlation between mass changes and phase transitions.
Separate ex situ TGA and XRD provide discrete datasets that may inadequately resolve transient interactions between oxidation and phase transformations.
Events occurring faster than the XRD scan frequency may not be fully resolved.
Measurement noise may mask subtle phase changes in the integrated experiment.

contradictions.description: The mechanism correctly assigns phase detection to XRD and mass-change detection to TGA, but the falsification rule refers to transient phase changes being observed in TGA. TGA alone does not directly identify phase changes, so this criterion conflicts with the stated division of measurement roles.
